text: Follow these guidelines to test that the notification area only shows public information and enables publicly accessible actions: - Work with developers or application designers to figure out the types of information shown in the notification area. - Create situations in which those notifications are shown. - Test if any private information is shown on the lock screen. - This test __fails__ if any private information is shown. - Test that custom critical actions are not enabled in the locked mode. - For example, it should not be possible to reply to messages in locked mode.

title: Test that use of Android third-party keyboards is managed
text: Use the following guidelines for testing that Android third-party keyboards are managed: - Identify input boxes that can be used to enter confidential or sensitive data, such as editable text boxes asking for passwords or personal information. - Install and use a third-party keyboard that is not well-known and is not in your application's whitelist. text: Use the following guidelines for designing a fallback mechanism or degraded mode for a system or application: The fallback system and degraded mode are activated when some components of the system fail, or when the resources are exhausted under attack. title: Verify that the system has a fallback mechanism or a degraded mode
text: Use the following guidelines for verifying that the system has a fallback mechanism, or a degraded mode, that allows critical services of the system to survive Denial of service (DoS) attacks, and other selected failures. - Simulate excessive resource consumption, DoS attacks, or those selected failures. - Test that the system can (minimally) operate in those situations. - Test that the essential/emergency functions are accessible in those cases.

title: Protect peripheral devices against malicious remote activation
text: Follow these guidelines to protect peripheral devices against malicious use: - Disable remote device activation except for specific devices that need this feature. Don't allow remote entities, or activate the device or components of the device, unless it is necessary. - Display a signal that indicates the device is being used. For example, turn on an LED light to indicate the camera is in use, or display an on-screen indicator that shows a certain resource is shared with another account. - Ensure that the information collected by the device is only accessible to authorized users or processes.

title: Verify that peripheral devices are protected against malicious remote activation
text: Follow these instructions to verify that peripheral devices are protected against malicious use: - Maintain a list of devices that are required to be activated through remote access. - Attempt to remotely activate each device. - This test __fails__ if there is no explicit indicator signaling when the device is activated. - Attempt to remotely activate the devices that are not on the list. - This test __fails__ if you can successfully activate a device.

title: Sign audit records for non-repudiation
text: Use the following guidelines for signing audit records for non-repudiation: - Whenever non-repudiation is a goal, ask the other entity to sign audit records with their private key and hold the records for a reasonable amount of time. - Use a secure digital signature algorithm for signing data. - Such as SHA512 with RSA, or SHA512 with ECDSA. - [NIST FIPS PUB 186-4 Digital Signature Standard (DSS)](http://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.186-4.pdf) provides an in-depth description of DSS algorithms. - Include time-stamps and identifiers in the audit records that are signed.

title: Verify that audit records are signed to enable non-repudiation
text: Verify that for every action that requires non-repudiation: - The log records are signed using the private keys of the involved entities that need to be held responsible. - A strong digital signature algorithm is used for signing data - Such as SHA512 with RSA, or SHA512 with ECDSA. - Time-stamps and identifiers are included in the audit records.

text: Use the following guidelines to check the size of incoming messages for services: - Perform load testing for services to make sure they are not vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks as a result of unrestricted incoming message sizes. - There are different load testing tools available to check whether the maximum size of payload is configured for the services. text: Follow these guidelines to secure the application in Doze/Standby or battery saving modes: - Identify time-critical functions of the app, and develop those functions in a way that is not affected by those modes. - Android offers two types of power saving modes: [Doze and Standby](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby.html). - The application goes to Doze mode after being idle for a significant amount of time. title: Implement update capabilities for your application
text: Implement update capabilities for your application to make sure it can be updated and patches can be applied quickly when vulnerabilities are discovered. Consider the following guidelines: - Provide both automatic and manual updates. Both should be considered to give users the freedom to update their applications/devices by choice, or to set it up to be done automatically. - Provide a capability for scheduled updates. title: Verify that all the components are authenticated explicitly
text: Verify that your application authenticates all other components explicitly before any kind of network communication with them. Additionally, ensure that it does not rely on an implicit trust of other components.

title: Test that your application provides update capabilities
text: Set up an update server for testing the following cases using the application: - Test that you can update your application manually. - Test that you can set your application to be updated automatically, and that it works as expected. - Test that you can schedule your application to be updated at specific time intervals, and that it works as expected.

text: Use the following guidelines for iOS notification settings: - Use the `getNotificationSettingsWithCompletionHandler:` method of the shared `UNUserNotificationCenter` object to get the most recent authorization status of your app. The method returns a `UNNotificationSettings` object whose contents reflect your app's current authorization status and the current notification environment. If push notifications are considered critical to the nature of your application: - Check its to-user-device delivery status. - Communicate its importance to the user using in-app pop-up messages.

title: Check authorization status before handling iOS app notification's custom action
text: Perform authorization status checks while handling a notification's custom action. Use the same degree of authentication and authorization for the application's security requirements.

title: Test your executables using publicly available reverse engineering tools
text: Use publicly available decompilers to reverse your executables to make sure you have hardened your code against reverse engineering to a fair degree.

title: Mitigate Deadlock and Recursion in Services
text: Use the following best practices to mitigate deadlock and recursion: - Use execution flow diagrams to mitigate service deadlock and recursion, especially within the domain of single application. - At the design level, use asynchronous service-to-service calls and message buffering. title: Verify that your iOS application checks for authentication before handling Siri intent
text: Use the following guidelines for verifying that your iOS application checks for authentication before handling Siri intents: Inspect the code and find handler methods. title: Test that your Android application checks for rooted devices and security/compatibility of the environment
text: Follow these steps to test that your application checks the runtime parameters and security requirements of the environment: - Install your application on a rooted Android device and test if the application detects it. - Run the application in an emulator and test that your application can detect the emulator. - Run the application in a debuggable mode, and test if the application detects it.

title: Test that your mobile application checks its integrity and installation source
text: Use the following guidelines for testing that your mobile app checks its integrity and installation source: 1. Install your application on a mobile device without using the default application store. Test that your application detects that it is not installed from the default source and changes its behavior according to the requirements. 2. Change the application slightly and create a new installation file. Install the application on a mobile device, and try to run it. If the application runs normally and there are no runtime integrity check errors, this test fails.

title: Enforce the principle of least privilege
text: The principle of least privilege is the concept that all subjects of a computing environment are restricted from accessing resources that are not essential to their purpose. This includes application components, users, and processes. Following this principle, additional processes, roles, and accounts should only be created as necessary. To enforce the fewest privileges on a subject, all privileges must be: - Restricted as much as possible. - Granted as late as possible. - Revoked as soon as possible.
